text: YouTube Data API: search.list has its own quota bucket of 100 calls/day, each call costs 1, separate from the 10,000-unit/day default pool for other endpoints
final_value: search.list: own bucket, default 100 calls/day, 1 quota per call (pagination calls each count); all other endpoints share 10,000 units/day by default; videos.insert also has its own 100/day bucket; quotas reset at midnight PT. Page last updated 2026-10-15 UTC.
note: Raw HTML re-read; wording matches the researcher's quote. The old '100 units per search call' model no longer applies.

text: Instagram Creator Marketplace API exists; launch date 2025-10-01 (Facebook Creator Discovery API 2025-10-06)
final_value: Instagram Creator Marketplace API GA 2025-10-01; Facebook Creator Discovery API GA 2025-10-06
note: The blog post says app review is required for the new permissions. The docs page, not the blog, carries the standard/advanced-access detail.

text: Instagram Creator Marketplace API access requirements: permissions, advanced access via app review, brand eligibility, rate limit
final_value: Facebook Login permissions: instagram_creator_marketplace_discovery, instagram_basic, pages_manage_metadata, pages_show_list, business_management. The discovery permission needs advanced access via app review; new apps get standard access automatically, which returns test data only. Meta checks brand eligibility at onboarding, and the brand must accept the Creator Marketplace ToS; a call from an ineligible brand returns error code 10. Needs a Page access token for a Page linked to the brand's Instagram business account (or a BISU token with Unified Login). Endpoint: GET https://graph.facebook.com/v25.0/<IG_USER_ID>/creator_marketplace_creators. Rate limit 5,000 requests per user per hour; app-level limit is 5,000 x effective users.
note: Adds the app-level rate limit and the Page/BISU token requirement, which the researcher did not state. The docs list no eligible countries or user types.

text: Threads API keyword search permission and limits
final_value: Requires threads_keyword_search (for GET on the keyword search endpoint) plus threads_basic. Until the app is approved for threads_keyword_search, search covers only the authenticated user's own posts. Limit: 2,200 queries per rolling 24 hours per user across all apps; repeat queries count, and queries returning no results do not count.
note: Researcher omitted the detail that zero-result queries do not count against the limit.

text: X API pay-per-use prices
final_value: Post reads $0.005/resource; user reads $0.010/resource; follower/following reads $0.010/resource; likes reads $0.001/resource; post create $0.015/request, or $0.200/request with a URL; counts: recent $0.005, all $0.010 per request. Pay-per-usage plans are capped at 3 million post reads per billing cycle, and higher volume needs Enterprise. The page says prices are subject to change and points to the Developer Console for current rates.

final_value: Free: $0, 100 credits, plus up to 7,000 bonus credits claimable. Freelance: $47 for 25,000 credits ($1.88 per 1k). Business: $497 for 500,000 credits ($0.99 per 1k). text: ScrapeCreators TikTok audience endpoint: path, cost, content

Returns audienceLocations[] with country, countryCode, count, percentage. Spec text: 'Right now you can only get the audience countries.' So the endpoint returns no age or gender.
note: The spec has 197 paths, matching the researcher.

text: SociaVault TikTok demographics endpoint and cost
final_value: GET https://api.sociavault.com/v1/scrape/tiktok/demographics, param handle (required), header X-API-Key, 26 credits per request. Returns audienceLocations[] with country, countryCode, count, percentage (a string such as '15.96%'). 'Currently includes audience country distribution', so no age or gender.
note: SociaVault packs (sociavault.com/pricing): Free Trial 50 credits; Starter $29 / 6,000 ($0.00483); Growth $79 / 20,000 ($0.00395); Pro $199 / 75,000 ($0.00265); Enterprise $399 / 200,000 ($0.00199). One-time packs, credits never expire. Pack figures were read through WebFetch's summariser and match the researcher's.

text: 'SociaVault is the only pay-as-you-go vendor with TikTok audience demographics'
final_value: False. At least three other vendors expose TikTok audience data. (1) ScrapeCreators: 26 credits, country only. (2) CreatorDB: POST https://apiv3.creatordb.app/tiktok/audience, param uniqueId, returns country shares (audienceLocations), gender (maleRatio/femaleRatio), average age and a 7-band age breakdown (13-17 to 65+); default request shows creditsUsed 1. (3) SocialCrawl: GET https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/tiktok/user/audience, 5 credits uncached, 0 if cached (30-minute cache); returns countries, and age, gender and state only when the creator has a public Shop marketplace card. Do not encode any 'only vendor' claim.
note: The researcher found only ScrapeCreators as a second vendor and missed CreatorDB (the only one with a full age/gender breakdown) and SocialCrawl. CreatorDB and SocialCrawl were read through WebFetch's summariser, and SocialCrawl's own page contradicts itself on whether age and gender are included. CreatorDB's credit pricing for a pay-as-you-go plan was not confirmed. TikHub: I grepped its OpenAPI for demograph/audience/portrait and found only the cookie-gated get_video_audience_stats.

text: TikHub has no profile-level TikTok audience demographics endpoint
final_value: A grep of TikHub's openapi.json paths containing 'tiktok' plus demograph/audience/portrait returned only /api/v1/tiktok/creator/get_video_audience_stats. The researcher said this endpoint needs the creator's own cookie, which I did not re-check.
note: Narrow check; I did not look at Douyin or other path patterns.

final_value: 197 paths, 200 operations (3 paths have GET+POST: /v1/facebook/adLibrary/search/ads, /v1/facebook/adLibrary/company/ads, /v1/reddit/post/comments). 36 paths accept cache_max_age; tiktok 29 paths, facebook 23, instagram 20, youtube 18.

final_value: GET /v1/tiktok/user/audience. Only param: handle (required). 26 credits per request. Returns audienceLocations[] (country, countryCode, count, percentage). Country only. No cache_max_age param.

text: find-creator-emails cost
final_value: GET /v1/find-creator-emails, params platform (required), handle (required), cache_max_age. Cost 1 credit if emails is empty (including successful partial-empty), 10 credits if any email is returned, 0 on cache hit, invalid input, missing source profile or failed lookup. Platforms: Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X/Twitter, Facebook.

text: find-social-profiles cost
final_value: GET /v1/find-social-profiles, params platform (required), handle (required), cache_max_age. 10 credits per successful live lookup. 0 on cache hit. The spec also says an uncharged 503 is returned if every declared link-in-bio page fails and nothing else yields a profile.

text: Instagram has a native profile search endpoint at v1/instagram/search/profiles
final_value: GET /v1/instagram/search/profiles, param query (required) only. Returns Instagram's first ranked native result set. Only the first 10 accounts are enriched (bio, links, counts). The rest keep only id, username, full name, verified flag, photo and URL. No pagination. Does not search Google-indexed bios or captions. The spec's own summary is 'Search Instagram Profiles'. Combined users, hashtags, places and suggestions are at /v1/instagram/search. The spec states no credit cost for this route, so assume 1 but treat it as unstated.
note: The pipeline's path v1/instagram/search/profiles is correct. Add the leading slash, because paths are /v1/... in the spec.

text: Skill pack paths that do not exist in the live combined spec, with replacements (exhaustive over every backticked /vN/ path in SKILL.md; 110 distinct paths checked, /v1/platform/action excluded as a pattern placeholder)
final_value: 6 hard fixes: (1) /v1/youtube/channel/videos -> /v1/youtube/channel-videos; (2) /v1/twitter/user/tweets -> /v1/twitter/user-tweets; (3) /v1/instagram/basic/profile -> /v1/instagram/basic-profile (param userId); (4) /v1/detect/age-gender -> /v1/detect-age-gender (param url); (5) /v1/credit/balance -> /v1/account/credit-balance (appears twice, in the table row and in the Credit Costs text); (6) /v1/tiktok/hashtags/popular -> REMOVE. It was retired 2026-07-16, no replacement. All 6 old paths return 404 live, except hashtags/popular, which still returns 401. The other 99 paths exist in the combined spec. Four further paths are not in the combined spec but are documented per-endpoint (see C10).
note: The researcher's file did not list this set. Fixes 1 to 5 are exact renames. Where the task wording implied replacements for every missing path, there is none for hashtags/popular, so it must be deleted, not renamed.

text: Skill paths /v1/reddit/ads/search, /v1/reddit/ad, /v1/tiktok/videos/popular, /v1/tiktok/songs/popular are absent from the combined spec
final_value: Absent from /openapi.json but still documented. They are listed in llms.txt, each has a working per-endpoint spec at https://docs.scrapecreators.com{path}/openapi.json (HTTP 200), and the live API returns 401 (route exists) for each. Keep them in the skill, flagged as 'in llms.txt and per-endpoint spec, not in the combined spec'. Params: reddit/ads/search: query (required), industries, budgets, formats, placements, objectives, max 30 ads. reddit/ad: id (required). tiktok/videos/popular: period, page, orderBy, countryCode. tiktok/songs/popular: page, timePeriod, rankType, newOnBoard, commercialMusic, countryCode, can take up to 30 s.
note: Do not delete these or rename them. Do not count them in the 197. I could not confirm they return data, because I have no API key. 401 only proves the route exists. The docs sidebar I saw does not list them. Whether they are live is unverified beyond the route and per-endpoint spec.

text: Skill's Credit Costs table (tiktok transcript '+10 credits when use_ai_as_fallback=true'; google company ads 25 when get_ad_details=true; audience 26)
final_value: /v1/tiktok/user/audience = 26 (correct). /v1/google/company/ads = 25 only with get_ad_details=true, otherwise 1 (correct). /v1/tiktok/video/transcript: native captions 1 credit only if returned, 0 if none. With use_ai_as_fallback=true, a successful AI transcript of 120 s or less costs a flat 1 credit. Over 120 s it is refused unless allow_long_transcription=true, which bills 10 credits per started minute (10*ceil(sec/60)) for ALL successful AI, even short ones. The skill's '+10 credits' is wrong.
note: Same AI pricing applies to /v1/facebook/post/transcript, /v1/twitter/tweet/transcript, /v2/instagram/media/transcript, Kick and Twitch clip transcripts and /v1/facebook/adLibrary/ad.

text: Other credit costs that differ from 1 and that the skill omits
final_value: download_media=true costs 10 credits if media is found, 1 otherwise, on /v1/instagram/post, /v2/tiktok/video and /v1/truthsocial/post. /v2/instagram/post/comments costs 1 per page with comments, or 15 with include_replies=true. Empty comment pages cost 0, and so do empty TikTok comment pages. /v1/instagram/profile: age-gated 403 or 'restricted/unavailable' 404 cost 0, legacy 200 'private/not found' placeholders cost 1. /v1/find-social-profiles 10. /v1/find-creator-emails 1 or 10. Cache hits (cache_max_age) cost 0. Dedicated native-caption transcript routes (TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, Rumble, LinkedIn) cost 1 only when a transcript is returned. /v1/youtube/video/transcript costs 1 and uses no AI.
note: Most endpoints do not state their cost in the spec. Cosmos endpoints state 1 credit per successful request. The skill's 'most endpoints cost 1' is consistent with the spec.

text: Skill: 'Transcripts: all transcript endpoints require video under 2 minutes'
final_value: The 120-second cap applies only to AI transcription, and it can be lifted with allow_long_transcription=true. TikTok native captions have 'no fixed length limit'. /v1/youtube/video/transcript: 'Videos of any length are supported when YouTube exposes public captions' and it does not use AI.

text: Skill header facts: '110 endpoints' and 'All endpoints use GET'
final_value: Combined spec has 197 paths / 200 operations (plus the 4 per-endpoint-only paths in C10). 3 paths also accept POST with a JSON body: /v1/facebook/adLibrary/search/ads, /v1/facebook/adLibrary/company/ads, /v1/reddit/post/comments. The docs' own pages still say '110+ endpoints', which is stale.

text: FTC Disclosures 101 key rules: disclosure must be hard to miss; 'ad', 'advertisement', 'sponsored' are adequate; vague terms like 'sp', 'spon', 'collab' and stand-alone 'thanks' or 'ambassador' are not; do not assume a platform tool is enough; in video the disclosure should be in the video, not only the description; disclosures behind a MORE click are likely missed; a hashtag such as #ad is 'fine (but not necessary)'.
final_value: Quotes: 'Place it so it's hard to miss.' | 'terms like "advertisement," "ad," and "sponsored"' are fine | 'Don't use vague or confusing terms like "sp," "spon," or "collab," or stand-alone terms like "thanks" or "ambassador"' | 'Don't assume that a platform's disclosure tool is good enough' | 'the disclosure should be in the video and not just in the description uploaded with the video' | likely missed 'anywhere that requires a person to click MORE' | 'It's fine (but not necessary) to include a hashtag with the disclosure, such as #ad or #sponsored' | 'Don't mix your disclosure into a group of hashtags or links'
note: The researcher's list omits 'ambassador' and the 'don't bury it in a hashtag group' rule. The page is dated November 2019.

text: 16 CFR Part 465 (FTC Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule) covers fake social-media influence indicators and took effect 2024-10-21.
final_value: 16 CFR 465.8 'Misuse of fake indicators of social media influence'. It is a violation to (a) sell or distribute, or (b) purchase or procure, fake indicators that the person 'knew or should have known to be fake' and that 'materially misrepresent their influence or importance for a commercial purpose'. Published 89 FR 68034 on 2024-08-22; effective 2024-10-21. The FTC authorizes civil penalties for knowing violations.
note: The effective date and substance are confirmed: the Federal Register API returns effective_on 2024-10-21, and the eCFR text was read. The researcher gave no section number (it is 465.8, not 465.7; 465.7 is review suppression) and wrote 'covers selling or buying' without the 'knew or should have known' and 'materially misrepresent ... commercial purpose' qualifiers, which a skill author should include. The eCFR page itself redirected the fetch tool, so I read the text through the eCFR versioner API (2026-10-29 snapshot).

text: FTC Q&A: hiring an influencer who happens to have fake followers is not by itself liability.
final_value: FTC staff answer: 'No.' The provision focuses on the 'distribution' of fake indicators to people who could use them to misrepresent their influence. A business buying fake indicators is liable only if it 'knew or should have known' they were fake (red flags). The rule 'went into effect on October 21, 2024'.
note: The researcher marked this Reported. I have now read the page, so it can be upgraded to confirmed. The FTC press release says 'knowing violators' face civil penalties and the vote was 5-0. No dollar amount appears on these pages.

text: Instagram: when the owner hides likes, like_count returns 0 when the media is queried indirectly.
final_value: Hidden likes: the 2021 changelog says an indirect query 'will now return 0' when the app user does not own the media and the owner hid likes. A direct query by the owner returns the real count. The current IG Media reference says like_count is omitted (not returned) when hidden and queried indirectly. Treat both 0 and missing as 'hidden/unknown', never as zero engagement.
note: The 2021 changelog matches the researcher. The current reference (developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/instagram-graph-api/reference/ig-media) describes omission instead, and says the owner can also hide comments, views, reposts and shares, so those fields may be omitted too. A skill that says 'returns 0' will miss the omitted-field case. Neither page names specific endpoints.

text: Instagram partnership label: Meta's Apr 2026 update lets apps set the 'Paid partnership' label via the Content Publishing API, but no read-side field for it is documented in Business Discovery or the Meta post.
final_value: Write-only: apps can publish with the 'Paid partnership' label (optionally 'Paid partnership with [Brand]'), for all media types including photos, Reels, carousels and Stories, via the Instagram API with Facebook Login. The blog post (dated 2026-04-22) names no read field. The Business Discovery docs list no partnership field (examples show id, comments_count, like_count, view_count and conditional media_url). The IG Media reference field list has no partnership, branded-content or sponsor field.
note: Confirmed absence in all three Meta pages. Whether the label can be scraped from the public web view is not established (unverified). Business Discovery returns no data for age-gated professional accounts. The IG Media reference says only professional-account media can be read. Business Discovery docs do not address private accounts.

text: Definition drift: Meta's Business Discovery view_count now combines Instagram and Facebook views for crossposted video (Apr 2026), and YouTube viewCount will count views when playback begins, including autoplay and hover, from Aug 24, 2026.
final_value: Meta (blog dated 2026-04-22): Business Discovery view_count returns combined Instagram and Facebook views for crossposted video. YouTube: from Aug 24, 2026, viewCount counts a view the moment a video begins to play, for long-form, Live and Shorts, including autoplay, hover and click-to-play.
note: Both read at the primary pages. Aug 24, 2026 is already past today (2026-11-02), so YouTube views-based baselines that span that date are not like-for-like.
